key_insight: A multi-modal machine learning ensemble predicted adverse ICU events after cardiothoracic surgery, but static preoperative registry data alone performed as well as the fused model.
clinical_relevance: This suggests hospitals can use existing preoperative variables to screen high-risk patients with strong negative predictive value, while intraoperative data mainly shifts the sensitivity-specificity trade-off.
method: Five-fold cross-validation on Society of Thoracic Surgeons registry data plus intraoperative time-series signals
Compared an ensemble of static and sequence models, including residual neural networks, CNNs, BiGRU, XGBoost, logistic regression, SVM, and gradient boosting
Evaluated separate modality models and per-signal ablations to test whether fusion added predictive value
evidence_signal: The balanced ensemble achieved AUC 0.87 with sensitivity 0.76, specificity 0.83, PPV 0.40, and NPV 0.96; static-only and time-series-only models reached AUC 0.87 and 0.83, respectively.
watch_item: Because the modalities were largely substitutable in this cohort and PPV was modest, performance should be externally validated before deployment and may not generalize across sites or workflows.
paper_title: PhysioFusion: A Multi-Modal Ensemble using Static Preoperative Variables and Time Series Intraoperative Data to Predict Adverse Events Following Cardiothoracic Surgery
